page: The UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-2xL4 is a KVM-hypervised virtual server configured with 12 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU configuration features 12 physical cores with single-thread execution, supported by 64 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. System memory totals 128.0 GB, providing 10.67 GB of RAM per core. Graphics and parallel computing acceleration are delivered via two NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined 48 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3942.28 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 42.79 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 45719.52 and a PassMark CPU score of 35206.69, reflecting the shared CPU allocation model. Memory bandwidth is stable, recording 146.11 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 89.37 GB/sec for large-block write operations. For AI workloads, the system achieves a top-tier text generation speed of 349.81 tokens per second using a small 135M parameter LLM, while prompt processing operates at an average rate of 1842.33 tokens per second.

This server offers a specialized resource profile that balances high-capacity GPU acceleration and substantial memory density against a shared CPU allocation model. The absence of local storage requires external storage attachments, which should be factored into deployment architectures. Given the dual NVIDIA L4 GPUs and 128 GB of RAM, this configuration is highly suited for machine learning inference, small-scale LLM execution, data science pipelines, and GPU-accelerated rendering workloads that do not require dedicated, non-shared CPU cores.
